title: Read the decision signals using their returned field names
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the decision signals using their returned field names**

`evaluate_decision` returns the composed fields `disposition_lead`, `advances_goal` and `is_destructive` (see `harness/jev_packs.py::compose_decision_verdict`), not `lead`, `advanced` and `destructive`. These lookups therefore silently discard all three signals, which is visible as three null values in `gates-620.json` and the other new receipts. Use the actual returned keys when serializing and printing the signals; otherwise reviewers cannot inspect the probabilities and lead underlying the recorded investigate/escalate decisions without finding the separate ledger.

pr_title: #475: record per-attempt http_status and timestamps for panel and Jev calls
title: Preserve wire attempts across chat-level retries
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve wire attempts across chat-level retries**

When a panel or judge call retries after a reasoning-parameter rejection, `chat.py` invokes `transport.post()` twice inside one `chat_routed()` call. Resetting the collection on every POST discards the first request's attempts before the panel can consume them, so a real `[400, 200]` sequence is persisted as `[200]`, understating attempts and hiding recovered calls. The same problem affects the affordable-budget retry. Initialize the collection at the logical call boundary and preserve it across the constituent POSTs.

pr_title: #475: record per-attempt http_status and timestamps for panel and Jev calls
title: Isolate the strict Jev call from previous wire traces
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Isolate the strict Jev call from previous wire traces**

When a strict Jev assessment follows an ordinary chat POST in the same context, this `record_call()` can consume the chat request's leftover wire attempts: `HttpTransport.post()` now always populates `_WIRE`, ordinary chat callers do not consume it, and `post_once()` neither resets nor records it. Consequently, `evaluate_vision_assessment()` can persist a `jev_eval` whose summary says HTTP 200 but whose attempt timeline contains an unrelated chat response and timestamps. This is reproducible with a chat POST returning 401 followed by a successful `evaluate_once()`, which records attempt statuses `[401]`. Give the one-attempt transport path its own fresh collection and record its actual attempt.

pr_title: docs(intake): file the keyless-vocabulary contract gap (#413)
title: Verify the vocabulary endpoint before recording a contract gap
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the vocabulary endpoint before recording a contract gap**

The cited probe calls `POST /api/driver/step`, not the keyless vocabulary endpoint. At this commit, `harness/server.py:2557-2570` ignores the supplied `action` field and always invokes `adapter.step()`, so `action: vocabulary` still runs the model-backed decision pipeline. Vocabulary retrieval instead uses `GET /api/driver/vocabulary` (`harness/server.py:1888-1889,2528-2531`), whose implementation in `driver_core/server.py:152-153` returns the vocabulary without making a decision. Consequently, the observed refusal does not establish the contract violation recorded here; correct the probe and disposition before adding this as a distinct open defect under #413.

pr_title: #476: record each ceiling refusal with the refused call's outcome
title: Distinguish post-dispatch overruns from calls refused before dispatch
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Distinguish post-dispatch overruns from calls refused before dispatch**

When `record_actual` rejects a billed response, `_record_refusal` still writes `outcome="refused"`, which this change defines as the call not having run. These calls have already run: `tests/test_spend.py::test_unreserved_inflight_overspend_documented` exercises this case, and `JevPolicy._account` can even retain the paid result after the accounting rejection. Task-scope checks reached from `record_actual` or `reconcile` have the same problem. Distinguish accounting overruns from pre-dispatch refusals so the new trace does not classify executed, billed calls as calls prevented by the ceiling.

pr_title: #476: record each ceiling refusal with the refused call's outcome
title: Include the binding scope's budget in scope-refusal events
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include the binding scope's budget in scope-refusal events**

When a task allowance rather than the session ceiling rejects a call, only the scope label reaches `_record_refusal`; its structured envelope always contains the global governor's numbers. For example, a $0.02 reservation rejected by a $0.01 task scope under a $1 session records `requested=0.02`, `phase_ceiling=1.0`, and `phase_remaining=1.0`, with no structured scope allowance or scope balances. Consumers replaying or classifying the refusal therefore see an amount that fits the recorded envelope and must parse the rounded human-readable reason to recover the actual constraint. Include the rejecting target's allowance, spent, and outstanding balances in the event.

pr_title: fix(flush): wire the campaign trace writer at the product entry (#469)
title: Handle trace initialization failures without aborting campaigns
body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle trace initialization failures without aborting campaigns**

If the configured trace ledger exists but cannot be read (for example, due to permissions or invalid UTF-8), `AutonomyLedger.__init__` raises from `_load()` before the campaign executes. The exception handling in `DecisionTrace.record()` cannot catch this because the writer has not yet been constructed. This makes previously independent campaign replays fail because an optional, non-audit trace sink is unavailable, contrary to the documented fail-open behavior. Handle initialization failures as well as append failures so an unavailable trace ledger does not prevent the campaign from running.
